data.assessment: In this rush period the town delivered 213.6 of 222.8 orders on time (0.96) with nothing unfinished. A is the weakest company at 0.93: it never waits on the road but loses 944 blocked seconds, about half of the town's 1888, mostly to B and C robots parked at node 8. Release-deadline overstays (20.8) are the largest violation cause. C is fully on time but carries most of the sanctions (13.7), which is why C (and B) resist rules that evict or penalise parked robots sooner.

proposals.title: block_k 3 -> 2 (evict a parked robot when two robots wait behind it)
proposals.rationale: A's 944 blocked seconds and its 0.93 on-time rate (the town's lowest) come from robots parked on the road. Two earlier measurements of block_k 2 showed +9.2 and +7.2 on-time deliveries (5/5 seeds), fewer late deliveries and a higher worst-company rate, so a similar gain is expected in this rush period. As before, A is expected to vote yes and B and C no, because C loses utility (about 65.8 -> 56.3 in period 2) and road violations rise. Nothing about the vote has changed, so the proposal is re-submitted only so that this period's measurement, including sanction_total, can go with the quorum referral (D1.f3) to the regulation officer.
proposals.cadl:
# =====================================================================
# robot_town.cadl ─── ロボットの街：3 社の配送ロボットが道路を共有する
#
# 道路網はラズパイマウスのシミュレータと同じ 11 ノード・17 エッジ。
# 3 社（A / B / C）が 2 台ずつロボットを走らせ、ノードは 1 台ずつしか
# 使えない。仕事のないロボットは車庫に戻るか、道路上（中央の交差点 8）
# に止まって次の注文を待つ。止まったロボットは他社の通行をふさぐ。
#
# `# @amend:<名前>` が付いた行は、改正してよいパラメータ。どの層（規則・
# 契約）に属し、どこまで動かしてよいかは constitution.yaml が決める。
# 委員会（COUNCIL）が自分で改正できるのは規則の層だけで、契約の層を
# 変えるには人間の判断が要る。
# =====================================================================

sos:
  name: "RobotTown"
  type: Collaborative             # 独立した 3 社が共通の規則を決める
  version: "1.0.0"

  context:
    environment:
      num_robots:   6
      num_companies: 3
      time_step_ms: 1000

  actors:
    - id: TOWN_STEWARD
      role: "road_steward"
      autonomy: low
      capabilities: [assign_order, record_violation, evict]
      interface:
        input:  [order_request, position_report, node_released, rule_update]
        output: [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, violation_report]

    - id: "ROBOT[1..N]"
      role: "delivery_robot"
      autonomy: high
      capabilities: [move, park, pickup, dropoff]
      interface:
        input:  [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, amendment_proposal]
        output: [position_report, node_released, ballot]

    - id: COUNCIL
      role: "rule_amendment_body"
      autonomy: medium
      capabilities: [propose_amendment, tally_ballots]
      interface:
        input:  [violation_report, ballot]
        output: [amendment_proposal, rule_update]

  contracts:
    # ── 顧客への約束：注文 1 件ごとのインスタンス（契約の層。人間が決める） ──
    - id: DELIVERY_SLA
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]"]
      guarantee:
        - "pickup_time <= 120s"         # @amend:pickup_deadline
        - "dropoff_time <= 120s"        # @amend:dropoff_deadline
      lifecycle:
        states: [Assigned, PickedUp, Delivered, Late]
        initial: Assigned
        terminal: [Delivered, Late]
        transitions:
          - id: pickup
            from: Assigned
            to:   PickedUp
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == PickedUp"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:pickup_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }
          - id: dropoff
            from: PickedUp
            to:   Delivered
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == Delivered"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:dropoff_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }

    # ── 道路の使い方：道路上に止まるたびに 1 インスタンス ──
    - id: ROAD_USE
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]", COUNCIL]
      guarantee:
        - "hold_time <= hold_limit"
      authority:
        decision_holder: COUNCIL
        beta: 0.5
        mode: "collective"
      information:
        alpha: 1.0                    # 規則と違反記録は全社に公開
      incentives:
        type: sanction
        lambda: 0.5                   # @amend:sanction_lambda
        rules:
          - "penalty(ROBOT[i], lambda) when overstay"
      lifecycle:
        states: [Holding, Overstay, Released, Evicted]
        initial: Holding
        terminal: [Released, Evicted]
        transitions:
          - id: release
            from: [Holding, Overstay]
            to:   Released
            on:   "ROBOT[i] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
            deadline: 60s             # @amend:hold_limit
            on_violation: { transition: Overstay, severity: Minor }
      monitors:
        - id: blocking_guard
          observe: "ROBOT[i].blocking"
          sampling: periodic(1000ms)
          rule: "ROBOT.blocking >= 2 AND state IN [Holding, Overstay]"  # @amend:block_k
          on_match: { transition: Evicted, severity: Major }

  # ── 運用モード：分散（各社が道路上で待つ）⇄ 集中（管理者が待避所を割り当てる） ──
  # 条件は 5 分ごとに、直前 5 分の観測で判定する。
  #   orders_in_window : 3 社の注文の合計件数
  #   blocked_pct      : ロボットが止まっているロボットにふさがれていた時間の割合（%）
  # 集中管理は交差点をふさがれない反面、エッジを 1 台ずつ割り当てるので、
  # 注文が非常に多いと許可待ちが積み重なる。そのときだけ分散に戻す。
  transitions:
    - from: DISTRIBUTED
      to: CENTRALIZED
      condition: "orders_in_window < 22"      # @amend:to_central
      protocol: SWITCH
      safety_invariant: "robots_on_road == 0"
    - from: CENTRALIZED
      to: DISTRIBUTED
      condition: "orders_in_window >= 26"     # @amend:to_distributed
      protocol: SWITCH

  protocols:
    - id: SWITCH
      trigger: "regime_condition_holds"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> ROBOT[*] : regime_notice"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
        - "TOWN_STEWARD : activate_regime"
    - id: AMEND
      trigger: "period_end"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> COUNCIL : violation_report"
        - "COUNCIL -> ROBOT[*] : amendment_proposal"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> COUNCIL : ballot"
        - "COUNCIL : tally_ballots"
        - "COUNCIL -> TOWN_STEWARD : rule_update"

  metrics:
    - id: on_time_deliveries
      formula: "count(Delivered)"
      target: ">= 0.9 * count(orders)"
    - id: blocked_time
      formula: "sum(blocked_robot_seconds)"
      target: "<= 600s"
proposals.why_human: B and C have voted this down twice and are expected to again, so it can only be adopted through the quorum referral (D1.f3). That referral is a regulation-layer decision. The operator asked that road_violations, C's utility loss and sanction_total be stated before it, and this period's measurement supplies them.
assumptions: Under rush-period traffic, the effect of block_k 2 resembles the period 1 and period 2 measurements.
B and C still vote on own utility, which falls from more evictions (Major) and fewer convenient parking spots.
unknowns: sanction_total under block_k 2 in a rush period.
Whether C's on-time rate (1.00) drops when its robots are evicted more often.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: Earlier measurements were +7 to +9 with 5/5 seeds.

predictions.subject: metric:min_company_on_time_rate
predictions.note: A (0.93) is the company being blocked.

predictions.subject: vote:C
predictions.note: C's utility fell about 9.5 in period 2.

proposals.title: hold_limit 60 -> 50 s (shorter allowed parking on the road)
proposals.rationale: Release-deadline overstays (20.8) and A's 944 blocked seconds show that robots park too long at the central node. A shorter hold limit is a milder alternative to block_k 2 that has not been measured yet: it should cut blocking for A and modestly raise town on-time, but it adds Minor sanctions for B and C. The votes are uncertain. A gains, while B and C trade fewer blocked seconds against more overstay penalties, so this is mainly a test of whether a gentler lever can pass by vote without an override.

regulation_proposals.title: vote.quorum 2 -> 1 (refer block_k 2 to the regulation officer, D1.f3)
regulation_proposals.rationale: In three measurements across normal and rush periods, block_k 2 raised town on-time by about 7 to 9 orders and lifted the worst company. It is blocked only because B and C vote on their own utility, and the sanction-only compensation route failed on customer grounds in D2. With quorum 1, a rule that passes the check, the invariants and the +1.0 on-time improvement gate could be adopted with one company's support. Customers gain fewer late deliveries and A's customers stop falling behind. A gains. B and C lose their veto: C's utility is expected to fall by about a seventh (65.8 -> 56.3 in period 2), B's by less, and both face more eviction sanctions. All three companies, including A, would also be exposed to future one-company rules that shift utility while still raising town on-time.
assumptions: The objective gate (min_improvement 1.0) and the invariants remain in force, so quorum 1 cannot adopt a change that lowers town on-time.
The regulation officer, not the operator, decides this, as stated in D1 and D2.
unknowns: sanction_total under block_k 2 in a rush period; this period's measurement of proposal 1 should supply it.

Whether a lower quorum lets future amendments raise town on-time while pushing one company's rate down toward the 0.6 floor; raising invariants.min_company_on_time_rate together with this change could limit that risk.
The long-term effect on companies' willingness to cooperate.

predictions.subject: metric:utility_gap
predictions.note: Uncertain: C's utility falls toward A and B's levels.
